newsitem.title: UK: Russia sets $1.0 bln five-year Eurobond, +345 bp.
newsitem.headline: Russia sets $1.0 bln five-year Eurobond, +345 bp.

text.p: Russia launched a $1.0 billion five-year Eurobond on Thursday, the country's first international bond offering since the 1917 revolution.
The Eurobond will be priced to yield 345 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, joint lead managers J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg said.
The size of the Eurobond exceeded market expectations, which originally were for up to $500 million. As recently as Wednesday, bankers were expecting the bond to total $750 million.
The increases followed an extensive marketing campaign by high-ranking Russian officials and bankers, who have toured the globe in the past two weeks.

A number of hurdles needed to be overcome before the issue could be launched. These included the Russian presidential elections mid-year, credit ratings from the key rating agencies and president Boris Yeltsin's recovery after his heart surgery. Yeltsin said he was in a "fighting mood" on Wednesday.
Also on Wednesday, Russian officials released some MinFin domestic bonds, which had been frozen.
Russia is rated Ba2 by Moody's Investors Service and BB minus by Standard & Poor's, which are below investment grade but were at the top end of market expectations when assigned in October.
